acceptance_results.element: Recommend the strongest for shock, curiosity and relevance; never default to the mildest
acceptance_results.evidence: Every set scores all three candidates 0-5 on shock, curiosity and relevance, prints the three numbers and a total, and names a recommendation with a written rationale.
acceptance_results.counts: 12/12 score rows arithmetic-correct (a+b+c == total). 4/4 recommendations are at the maximum total. 4/4 recommended candidates are not the mildest in their set.
acceptance_results.per_set: A: totals A1=13, A2=12, A3=15 -> recommended A3 (15, max). B: B1=14, B2=12, B3=13 -> recommended B1 (14, max). C: C1=15, C2=12, C3=14 -> recommended C1 (15, max). D: D1=14, D2=14, D3=14 -> three-way tie, recommended D2; the tie-break is written as the image ('a ceiling falling over a crib is the only one of the three that cannot be explained away as a misunderstanding'), not as the soft option.
acceptance_results.rule_stated: references/sensational-openings.md section 7 states the rule in the imperative: 'Recommend the strongest candidate. Never default to the mildest. A safe opening that everyone can live with is the failure mode this file exists to prevent', and adds that sliding to the soft version is not compliance.

acceptance_results.element: The invented-event prohibition is removed for fiction and retained for factual claims
acceptance_results.evidence_removed_for_fiction: references/sensational-openings.md adds section 7.1 'Invented catastrophe is permitted in drama', which states 'There is no blanket rule here prohibiting invented catastrophic events in fictional or composite drama. This doctrine supersedes any such reading', lists the events a composite character may suffer (job, house, marriage, business, eviction, denial, foreclosure, recall, malpractice, betrayal, collapse) and says none is off-limits for being too severe. It also names the mildness reflex as the defect rather than as compliance.
acceptance_results.evidence_removed_at_the_prior_site: references/stage-runbook.md, FU-U16 story doctrine section, carried the phrase 'compelling true stories' (line 174). The delta commit inserts a 'Clarification (S75X-W1-U2)' directly beneath it (lines 179-188): 'True in this section means emotionally true and dramatically honest, not factually verified. There is no blanket rule against invented catastrophic events in fictional or composite drama', with the factual-claim ban restated in the same paragraph. The prohibition was therefore neutralised at the exact place it was readable, not only in a new file.
acceptance_results.evidence_retained_for_factual_claims: section 7.2 'The boundary that does not move' keeps the ban: no invented event or outcome presented as a verified fact about a real person or product; no real client, employee, doctor, officer or official named or depicted as the villain; no 'verified' / 'real customer' / 'actual results' / 'studies show' label over fiction; no invented review, testimonial, case result, award, licence or statistic. The veto list in section 7 makes 'the invented event is presented as a verified fact about a real person or real product' an override of the score, and section 10 reviewer check 6 tests it. Labelling is specified: FICTIONAL_PLOT_EVENT for invented plot events, COMPOSITE for invented characters, CLIENT_SUPPLIED_TRUE for client-supplied true stories.
